First: a correction to the record
Your memory of this project said Slice 47 and 1166 tests. The tree says Slice 51 and 1223 tests, all green. I reconstructed the working tree from dump.txt — 360 file records, 359 matching their SHA-256 exactly (the one exception is LICENSE, which the dump elides by design since Slice 46). claude-terminal.txt confirms total: 1223, failed: 0 twice, seventeen E2E scenarios passing, every local CI gate green.

So Slices 47–51 shipped: section resequencing, item resequencing, the guest heading description, MenuGrouping plus the kitchen's grouped 86 panel, and Stage 4a (the menu_item_image schema, ImageFormat, ADR-0015). Stage 3 is closed. This is Slice 52 and it is Stage 4b.

What Slice 52 is
The carried item named in Slice 51 was blunt: no surface reads or writes a picture. Stage 4b discharges it.

The open design question is settled. The plan named two options for getting a file into a static-SSR page — a multipart form posting to a minimal API endpoint, or making a page interactive. There is a third that neither named and it is better than both: a plain <form enctype="multipart/form-data" @formname=… @onsubmit=…> posts to the page itself, and the handler reads HttpContext.Request.Form.Files. Blazor's static form dispatch reads Request.Form anyway, so antiforgery stays the framework's job, post/redirect/get is unchanged, and the page stays static SSR.

The size cap stays in one place. No transport ceiling is restated in C# — Kestrel's existing 30 MB body limit already bounds every POST this application accepts, so the picture form introduces no new number. A four-megabyte phone photo is refused by §8.2's named CHECK and reported by constraint name, exactly as designed.

A finding: F-102. AttachMenuItemImageOutcome's summary says "Six answers rather than a boolean" — and the enum has seven members, three lines below the sentence counting them. Found by reading the type in order to write the surface that renders one sentence per member (F-93's timing, third occurrence). Repaired by deleting the number per F-77, not correcting it.

Done so far
src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Menu/MenuItemImageEndpoints.cs — new: MenuImageRoutes (keyed on the image identifier, which is what makes immutable truthful), MenuItemImageUpload (field name + accept derived from ImageFormat.RecognisedContentTypes, so F-80's vocabulary is not declared a third time), and the anonymous GET endpoint.
MenuWorkflow.cs — both verbs behind IMenuWorkflow, publishing on a written row only, keyed on the two success outcomes rather than "not a refusal".
OrdersServiceCollectionExtensions.cs, Program.cs, MenuItemImages.cs (F-102).
Remaining
ManageMenuItem.razor (the picture panel), app.css (.manage-picture* — needed, or an unconstrained <img> breaks §16.3 scenario 16 at 375px), the new MenuItemImageSurfaceContractTests (6 facts), MenuWiringTests (+3), ContentSecurityPolicyContractTests (+1 — the "no CSP change needed" fact Slice 51 promised), TestingSectionContractTests (MinimumCountedClasses 27→28), then §7/§11.4/§11.11/§16.4/Appendix A/changelog v1.37, the plan, the ledger, BUILD_PROGRESS.md, _CHANGES.md, and the tar.

Predicted test count: 1223 → 1233. Files to delete: none. git add will be needed for two new files.

The correction first
Your memory said Slice 47 and 1166 tests. The tree says Slice 51 and 1223, all green — settled by reconstructing the working tree from dump.txt (360 records, 359 SHA-256 matches; LICENSE is elided by design). Slices 47–51 shipped both resequencing verbs, the guest heading description, MenuGrouping with the kitchen's 86 panel, and Stage 4a. Stage 3 is closed.

The menu progress
The transport question is settled, and the answer is neither option the plan named. A plain enctype="multipart/form-data" form posts to the page itself under an ordinary @formname, and the handler reads HttpContext.Request.Form.Files. That costs nothing because Blazor's static form handling has already read the body in order to find _handler and dispatch — the request the model binder declined to bind one field of is sitting there, cached. A minimal API endpoint would have acquired a second authorization rule that has to agree with the page's; an interactive page would have put a circuit under §11.4's largest form surface to move one file.

GET /menu/image/{id} is anonymous, 404s for a picture since replaced, and sets immutable — true rather than hopeful, because the route is keyed on the image. Attach and remove come behind IMenuWorkflow, discharging the obligation Slice 51 re-opened by name, publishing on the two outcomes that wrote a row rather than on "not a refusal".

No number was added anywhere. §8.2's named CHECK is still the only cap; the bound on what the process buffers is the one every other POST already inherits.

The finding — F-102
AttachMenuItemImageOutcome's summary said "Six answers rather than a boolean". The enum has seven members, three lines below — and the sentence saying six is the sentence arguing that no answer may be collapsed. Deleted rather than corrected per F-77; F-93's timing for the third time.

One thing worth flagging
My §16.4 gate simulation caught a real F-70: MenuWiringTests was cited at 23 assertions and my three new facts made it 26. Corrected in the same archive. The floor moves 27 → 28.

Two things to check first on a red run
Whether Blazor's static form handling dispatches a multipart post. Load-bearing for the whole transport decision. Symptom if wrong: the handler never runs, the page re-renders with no flash and no error. Fallback is the minimal API endpoint, at the cost of a second authorization rule.
Whether Request.Form.Files[name] returns null rather than throwing for an absent part.
Next
Stage 4c — the guest's menu, which is the half actually asked for: a thumbnail beside the name, loading="lazy", and an alt_text column. Still deferred by name: browser-side downscaling, now the thing that decides whether this feature is usable at all.
